meta.topic: Watch power sources: quartz battery life, solar and automatic movements, what a dead battery left in does, maker battery-replacement services and prices, and service intervals for automatics
meta.fitsCatalog: Researched against the 50 products with category 'watches' in src/engine/content/clothingcatalog.ts. Every one of them is listed under models[] by its catalog id. The brief named 13 brands. The catalog also sells Thomas Sabo, Nine West, CLOE, Puma, Folio and York Team Polo Club watches, and those are listed too.

conventions.confirmed: true only when the figure or fact was read on the maker's own page, manual or price list on the read date. false when it came from a search-engine summary, a retailer, or a blocked maker page. The note says which.
conventions.batteryLifeYears: A number, a [min, max] range, or null. On a model it is filled only when the maker gives a figure for that model, module or caliber. Otherwise it is null and the brand-level figure in brands[] applies. For solar and automatic watches it is null because they take no replaceable battery.
conventions.movement: quartz (replaceable battery), solar (light-charged rechargeable cell: Eco-Drive, Seiko solar), automatic (self-winding mechanical), or null when it could not be established.
conventions.nulls: A figure that could not be read is null and carries a note. No number here is estimated or invented.

meta.method: Maker pages were fetched directly with WebFetch or curl, and maker PDFs read with pdftotext. Casio, Fossil, Michael Kors, Cartier's FAQ and tommy.com refused fetches (403 or Cloudflare). For those, Casio's operation-guide PDFs and Cartier's care page did load. Where only a search summary was available the entry is confirmed:false.
meta.related: docs/research/world/research-jewelry-watches.json already holds the Tissot service price lists by market, Seiko USA's caliber-by-caliber service prices, Timex's mail-in fees and Seiko and Tissot service intervals. They are referenced here, not copied.

brands.basis: 'the battery in a quartz watch needs to be replaced every 2 to 5 years, depending on the model and usage'. The same page also says to change it 'approximately every 2 years or as recommended by the manufacturer'. Product pages give the cell but not its life: CR2016 (Easy Reader 35mm, Weekender 37mm), CR1216 (Easy Reader 25mm), CR2025 (IRONMAN Classic 30), SR920SW (Marlin Quartz GMT).
brands.leakage: 'A drained battery left inside a quartz watch can leak acid, which can corrode and ruin the movement.'
brands.serviceIntervalNote: For automatics: 'serviced every 3 to 5 years, or every 5 to 10 years, depending on the specific model and usage'. Timex gives both ranges in one sentence; it does not say which models fall in which.
brands.note: Read on timex.com's own blog. Timex's solar page says a solar watch's cell lasts 7-12 years on average, but that came from a search summary and no Timex solar watch is in the catalog.

brands.basis: Casio gives battery life per module in each operation guide, not per brand. Module 593 (F-91W): 'Approx. 7 years operation on type CR-2016 ... [assuming alarm operation for 20 sec./day and one light operation for 1 sec./day]'. LTP-1234 series: 3 years on SR626SW (casio.com spec, search summary only). See models[].
brands.leakage: Casio's manuals do not use the word leakage. They say 'Operation while battery power is low can result in malfunction. Replace the battery as soon as possible.' Casio America's repair terms list 'battery leakage' among the damage that triggers a revised estimate.

batteryService.kind: authorised service center or original retailer
batteryService.note: Casio publishes no battery price. Its US repair terms say out-of-warranty work is estimated in writing and 'rates vary between facilities'. The battery fitted at the factory is a test battery that 'may go dead quicker than the normally rated battery life', and replacing it is charged even within the warranty period.

brands.note: casio.com product pages returned 403. The manuals on casio.com's content server did load. Repair terms read at https://ecasiorepair.casio.com/terms/.

brands.basis: Module 3229 (DW-5600E): 'Approximately 2 years on type CR2016 (Assuming 3.5 seconds display illumination operation and 20 seconds alarm operation per day, Flash Alert enabled)'. 'Frequent use of the backlight shortens the battery life noted above.'
brands.leakage: Same Casio wording as above: replace a low battery as soon as possible, since operating on it can cause malfunction.

batteryService.kind: authorised service center or original retailer
batteryService.note: No published price. 'When replacing the battery, also request a check for proper water resistance.' A watch showing cracks when handed in for a battery is returned unserviced with an explanation.

brands.note: A search summary of the US DW-5600E-1V product page gave 5 years on CR2016 while the European page gave 2. The product page itself returned 403. The 2 years recorded here is the manual's.

brands.basis: 'This watch keeps operating for approximately 3 years if a new normal battery is inserted in it.' (Seiko quartz instruction, caliber A824). Seiko also says the battery fitted at the factory is a monitor battery whose life may be shorter.
brands.leakage: 'If the old battery is left in the watch for a long time, a malfunction may be caused due to battery leakage, etc.' The battery FAQ says to replace it promptly after it runs down to prevent damage from leakage.

batteryService.kind: Authorized Seiko Service Center or Seiko appointed dealer, with genuine Seiko batteries
batteryService.note: Seiko USA publishes no standalone battery price. A full analog quartz movement service is USD 100-135 and a V-series solar service USD 163, both including the battery or cell (research-jewelry-watches.json seiko-us-prices).

brands.serviceIntervalNote: 'we recommend having your watch serviced about every three years'. The solar FAQ says 'every 3 or 4 years', and that a rechargeable cell's capacity 'may gradually deteriorate' with long use.
brands.note: Also read: https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/customerservice/faq/repairs-4, https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/customerservice/faq/care-maintenance-1 and https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/customerservice/faq/solar1. Every Seiko in the catalog is automatic except one solar, so the quartz figure applies to none of them today.

brands.basis: Fossil's blog: 'The average watch battery duration is between 2 to 3 years', depending on type and functions. A Fossil Group support article says traditional watch batteries are 'expected to last 2 years from when they are replaced'.

batteryService.kind: Fossil Group mail-in repair portal (services-us.fossilgroup.com) or a Fossil store
batteryService.note: The portal lists a 'Battery' product for Fossil watches (SKU LG010, 'non-warranty') at USD 0 up front and says final charges come after inspection. A search summary of a Fossil Group article gave in-store battery replacement at GBP 25 / EUR 25 / CHF 25, with mail-in prices varying. That is not confirmed.

brands.note: fossil.com and support.fossilgroup.com sit behind a Cloudflare challenge and returned 403. The life figures come from search summaries limited to fossil.com and fossilgroup.com. The repair-portal product data was read directly (https://services-us.fossilgroup.com/products/fossil-watch-battery.js).

brands.basis: Quartz (non-Eco-Drive): Citizen's caliber list in the cal. 6031 instruction gives each caliber's battery life as 2, 3 or 5 years. Eco-Drive: 'Light seamlessly powers your watch without the need for battery replacements', running 'up to 6 months in complete darkness when fully powered'. Its rechargeable cell 'does not require periodical replacement'.
brands.leakage: 'If a worn down battery is left in your watch, it may cause a malfunction due to leakage of battery fluid and so on. Please make sure to replace the battery promptly.'

batteryService.note: Citizen does not recommend owners change their own batteries, and quotes repairs only after inspection. No battery price is published.

brands.serviceIntervalNote: Mechanical: 'Have the watch disassembled and cleaned (overhaul) every 2-3 years.' Eco-Drive: 'we recommend having your watch inspected every 2-3 years'. Power use rises as parts wear and oils age, which drains a stored charge faster.
brands.note: Also read: https://www.citizenwatch.com/us/en/technology-eco-drive, https://www.citizenwatch-global.com/support/pdf/8720/e.pdf (Eco-Drive cell and inspection), https://www.citizenwatch-global.com/support/pdf/0910/e.pdf (mechanical overhaul) and https://www.citizenwatch-global.com/support/simple_pdf/6850.pdf (SR927W, 'Average life is approximately 2 years').

brands.basis: Tissot's quartz product pages give the cell voltage (1.55 V) and an end-of-life indicator ('Tissot EOL'), but no battery life. Tissot says its Lightmaster solar cells last 10-15 years, which came from a search summary; no Lightmaster is in the catalog.

batteryService.kind: Tissot light service (battery at a minimum labour fee, parts extra)
batteryService.see: research-jewelry-watches.json tissot-prices: quartz light service USD 35, CAD 50, GBP 30, EUR 35 (IE), MXN 800, all confirmed on tissotwatches.com.

brands.serviceIntervalNote: 'we recommend that you have your watch serviced every 4 to 5 years by a Tissot Authorised Service Centre', plus a yearly water-resistance check.
brands.note: The battery life for the PRX quartz caliber (ETA) was not found; eta.ch did not respond.

brands.basis: 'the life span of the battery inside can be anywhere from one year to five years'. Longines quartz watches show end of life with a seconds hand that jumps every few seconds.

batteryService.note: From Longines' Canadian price list, which excludes tax and shipping. Quartz 2-3 hands: partial CAD 130, full 360. The UK list (GBP, VAT included) shows no battery-only line: quartz partial GBP 90, full 230, both including a battery. A search summary gave a Netherlands battery-only price of EUR 35 and an Australian one of AUD 70 (not read). The US price page returned 404.

brands.serviceIntervalNote: Services page: 'a full service is recommended every six to eight years.' The Longines blog says automatics should be serviced 'about every three to five years'. The two Longines pages disagree; both are recorded.
brands.note: Also read: https://www.longines.com/en-us/customer-service/services, https://www.longines.com/en-ca/customer-service/services/maintenance-prices and https://www.longines.com/en-gb/customer-service/services/maintenance-prices. Longines' English instruction manuals (api.ecom.longines.com) were read and give no battery life in years.

brands.basis: 'For quartz watches, the average battery life is at least three years.'
brands.leakage: 'We recommend that you do not leave a used battery inside your watch since it may cause rusting and damage the movement.'

batteryService.kind: Cartier battery service (battery and seals, water resistance restored)
batteryService.note: Takes at least one week. The FAQ says battery changes are not a same-day boutique service.

brands.serviceIntervalNote: 'We recommend a functional check every six years to verify the accuracy and reliability of your watch.' A search summary also quoted a Complete Service 'approximately every five years', which was not read on the page.
brands.note: Battery service price read at https://www.cartier.com/en-us/services/watches/our-watchmaking-services/care-and-repair/. The curl fetch was refused, but WebFetch loaded both pages.

brands.basis: Battery replacement: 'replacing the battery with a new one (depending on use, its lifespan can be between 6 months and 2 years) as well as changing the seals', followed by water-resistance testing and an ultrasonic clean.

batteryService.note: FC's list in CHF excluding VAT: quartz battery change 40, quartz partial service 145; mechanical partial 155, full 290; complicated automatic partial 225, full 455. 'Service centers may vary the price by +/- 20%, depending on the country, the exchange rate and the local tax system.'

brands.serviceIntervalNote: 'The servicing should be carried out every four years to ensure that the mechanism remains in good working order and lubricated.' The global maintenance page says to have water resistance checked every 3 years and the US page every 4.

brands.basis: 'Your quartz analog watch or chronograph has a battery specially designed for watches. It will last approximately 18-36 months under normal use.' Frequent use of the chronograph shortens it. On many models the seconds hand moves in 4-second steps when the battery is nearly exhausted.

batteryService.kind: Tommy Hilfiger Watches (Movado Group) service center, by mail
batteryService.note: Service request form B: battery USD 6.00 / CAD 15.00, shipping and handling USD 9.95 / CAD 14.95. In-warranty service carries USD 12.00 shipping and handling. One paragraph of the same file gives CAD 10.00 for the battery while the warranty paragraph and form B give CAD 15.00. Batteries are not covered by the 10-year limited warranty.

brands.note: Tommy Hilfiger watches are made under licence by Movado Group, and this is Movado's own operating, care and warranty file. Also read: the US/Canada limited warranty PDF on the same Movado server.

brands.basis: No Michael Kors or Fossil Group page giving a battery life for Michael Kors watches could be read. Fossil Group makes Michael Kors watches under licence, so Fossil's 2-3 years (unconfirmed) is the closest figure.

batteryService.note: services-us.fossilgroup.com lists an 'mkors-watch-battery' service with no up-front price (quote after inspection).

brands.note: michaelkors.com returned 403 to every fetch. Third-party guides give about 2 years, which are not recorded as figures.

brands.basis: No battery life published. Third-party listings name Miyota quartz movements on SR626SW cells (2115 in The Hexagon Phantom, 2039 in the Queen).
brands.serviceIntervalNote: Search summary of the Plein watch warranty: 'For perfect waterproofing it is advisable to have the watch serviced every 24 months.' The watches are warranted for 24 months by Timex Nederland B.V., and the battery is excluded.
brands.note: plein.com went into a redirect loop on every fetch, so the warranty text comes from a search summary.

notFound: Tissot quartz battery life (PRX, ETA caliber). Tissot pages give voltage and the EOL indicator only, and eta.ch did not respond.
Longines battery life per caliber. The English manuals give cell types (317-379, 1.55 V) and E.O.L./E.O.E. behaviour but no years. Longines' US price page returned 404.
Michael Kors battery life and leakage wording. michaelkors.com and Fossil Group's support site are behind Cloudflare.
Fossil's leakage wording, and a confirmed published battery price. The repair portal prices batteries at USD 0 up front, with the charge set after inspection.
Casio, Seiko (standalone) and Citizen battery-replacement prices. All three quote after inspection or leave it to dealers.
Philipp Plein battery life and service price. plein.com would not load.
Movement for the Nine West, CLOE, Puma, Folio and York Team Polo Club watches, the Citizen '60929' and the Tommy Hilfiger gift kit 2770242.

Leakage wording from Tissot, Longines, Frederique Constant, Michael Kors and Tommy Hilfiger. Their pages read here do not mention it. OMEGA (research-jewelry-watches.json), Seiko, Citizen, Cartier and Timex do.
worthChecking: Casio DW-5600E-1V battery life: the module 3229 manual says approx. 2 years on CR2016, while a search summary of the US product page said 5 years. Casio may have revised the module. Recheck the product page in a browser.
Frederique Constant FC-335MC4P6P at El Palacio de Hierro: the retailer says quartz, while FC's own page for FC-335MC4P6 says automatic FC-335. Recorded as automatic, unconfirmed.
Tommy Hilfiger Canadian battery fee: the same Movado file gives CAD 15.00 (warranty paragraph and form B) and CAD 10.00 (battery replacement paragraph).
Longines service interval: the services page says a full service every 6-8 years, while the Longines blog says automatics every 3-5 years.
Timex automatic service interval is given as '3 to 5 years, or every 5 to 10 years' in one sentence with no model split.

Every watch maker read here says the battery fitted at the factory is a test or monitor battery that may die before the rated life: Casio, Seiko and Citizen in their own words. Casio charges for replacing it even within warranty.

Simons (Citizen) and Coppel pages were unreachable, so the exact Citizen references sold there are not known. Rolan and Garrison are Eco-Drive lines on citizenwatch.com, but Citizen also sells non-Eco-Drive quartz in some lines.
